A player advocating for themselves for the Ballon d'Or is totally natural.

That being said, Kylian Mbappe's interviews are straight gaslighting.

The only reason he won the Golden Boot in the World Cup is because he faced a rotated England squad after Thomas Tuchel replaced seven players who started vs. Argentina.

Thomas Tuchel said:

“None of our players and none of the French players want to play this match. They want to play the final. We gave everything to achieve that. Everyone plays to win the World Cup, but that’s how it is. We have one less day of recovery than France, but we will do it with professionalism."

Imagine facing a squad that doesn't even want to be there (on one day less of rest) and STILL losing despite playing 90 minutes.

England's best players in Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham agreed to sit out. Mbappe refused in order to chase an award and that's the perfect encapsulation of Mbappe's season. Selfishness.

text:
陶哲轩于今日发表的这篇《A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics》具有重要意义。
该文联合了包括他在内的25位菲尔兹奖得主 发表共同宣言，核心指出 AI公司将攻克数学难题作为Benchmark的激进做法。

生产数学成果与培养数学家正在成为两件事。 
以前，资助人的成长是获得突破的必要投入。如果机器能够直接交付成果，这笔投入就需要重新证明价值。这是我认为声明背后最严峻的问题。
人类理解并非所有成果产生价值的前提。 一个证明可以先被严格验证，再被逐步理解。

但科学的价值也不止于确认某个命题为真。能否提炼出可迁移的方法，决定一次突破能否催生下一批突破。

难懂是否等于无用？
批量正确是否等于理论成熟？

判断力往往是做具体工作练出来的。 
如果训练任务被自动化，初级岗位随之消失，未来的专家从哪里来？
自动化最隐蔽的代价，可能是今天提高产出，十年后切断人才供给。
这个问题，人们无法靠几门提示词课程解决。

科学成果可能加速增长，科学家的职业机会却未必同步增长。 如果少数团队借助模型就能完成过去整个院系的工作，新增经费可能更多流向算力，而非职位。
知识繁荣与职业收缩完全可以同时发生。
技术进步，从未承诺按贡献历史分配收益。

决定未来格局的是独立验证的成本。
如果发现越来越便宜，复核却仍然昂贵，掌握算力的平台就可能同时成为成果生产者与事实裁判。
科学会拥有更多答案，却依赖更少的权威。
我支持AI加速科研，但进步必须允许被独立推翻。否则，我们得到的只是更强大的知识供应商。缺乏沉淀、伦理危机、传承断裂，都是需要认真思考的问题。

text:
We independently benchmarked Devin Fusion for its release today - this is the first time a multi-model coding agent has been included on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, and it effectively retains Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra performance while reducing costs

Devin Fusion runs a frontier lead model with a cost-efficient sidekick. We tested configurations from Cognition combining frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI with their new SWE-2 (medium) as a sidekick model. Configured with Claude Fable 5.1 (xhigh) + SWE-2 (medium), Devin Fusion scores 62 on the Coding Agent Index v1.5, while with GPT-6 Astra (xhigh) + SWE-2 (medium) it scores 59. The Fable configuration has the higher score, while the Astra configuration is 43% less expensive and completes tasks 31% faster.

Congratulations to @cognition on the release! See below for our results and analysis 🧵

现在人家孩子马上都要上幼儿园了，每次聚餐，我都无法直视他的老婆🤣因为，我没告诉他，手机微信里的照片删了，但是我无意中发现，电脑微信记录还在

quotedTweet.text:
SWE-bench 等公开基准被“刷爆”，Cursor 更新发布私有基准 CursorBench 4.0

· Claude Fable 5.1、Opus 5 贵但确实最强
· GPT-6 Astra 不参与评测（原因你懂）
· Grok 4.6 表现不突出，和 Muse Spark 1.3 相比优势不大，且更贵
· Lee 表示 Grok 4.7 会有很大提升

https://t.co/C8dMqi4ooG

再看看 CursorBench 方法论：从真实会话中“反向出题”
核心机制是 Cursor Blame：将已提交的代码追溯回生成它的智能体请求，天然形成“开发者查询—标准答案”配对。配套设计包括：
· 防泄漏：大量任务来自内部代码库和受控来源，且每隔数月整体更换题库；
· 任务更重：从初版到 3.0，任务规模（代码行数、涉及文件数）约翻倍，明显大于 SWE-bench 各变体，并引入 monorepo 多工作区、排查生产日志、长时实验等难题；
· 刻意保留歧义：任务描述保持简短、信息不充分，模拟开发者真实的表达方式，而非为方便评分而人为消除不确定性。

评测理念：线上-线下双闭环
CursorBench（线下）衡量正确性、代码质量、效率、交互行为多个维度；线上评估则在真实流量上做受控实验，专门捕捉“离线得分高、但开发者实际体验更差”的回归，这类问题是纯离线评测的盲区。

Cursor 给了一个消融实验案例：完全移除语义搜索工具后，才准确定位其价值集中在大型代码库的仓库级问答场景。

再看看 CursorBench 方法论：从真实会话中“反向出题”
核心机制是 Cursor Blame：将已提交的代码追溯回生成它的智能体请求，天然形成“开发者查询—标准答案”配对。配套设计包括：
· 防泄漏：大量任务来自内部代码库和受控来源，且每隔数月整体更换题库；
· 任务更重：从初版到 3.0，任务规模（代码行数、涉及文件数）约翻倍，明显大于 SWE-bench 各变体，并引入 monorepo 多工作区、排查生产日志、长时实验等难题；
· 刻意保留歧义：任务描述保持简短、信息不充分，模拟开发者真实的表达方式，而非为方便评分而人为消除不确定性。

评测理念：线上-线下双闭环
CursorBench（线下）衡量正确性、代码质量、效率、交互行为多个维度；线上评估则在真实流量上做受控实验，专门捕捉“离线得分高、但开发者实际体验更差”的回归，这类问题是纯离线评测的盲区。

Cursor 给了一个消融实验案例：完全移除语义搜索工具后，才准确定位其价值集中在大型代码库的仓库级问答场景。

Went fully back to Ghostty for my main setup, with VS Code on the side to look up code and Cursor/GPT-5 for reviews (sometimes also the cli).

VS Code's terminal is too unstable, had plenty freezes when pasting in large amounts of text. Nothing beats Ghostty.

Gemini can be great, but it's edit tools are too messy, so using it less and less. GPT-5 for reviewing plans works even better than Gemini.

Yes, all of these work on main. I tried the whole worktree setup, just slows me down. If you pick areas of work carefully you can work on multiple areas without much cross-pollination.

Claude often makes a mess but it's equally great in refactoring and cleaning up. Important to do both to not create too much technical debt.

Having the initial topic in the statusbar + session ID in case I need to switch accounts or restart a session is super helpful.

Using plan mode and iterating is key. Smaller tasks I do right away, bigger I write in a file and let GPT-5 review.

Wehen I'm not refactoring I usually tun 1-2 agents; for cleanup/tests/UI work ~4 seems to be the sweet spot. All depends on the blast radius of the work.

The hardest part is distrubuted system design, picking the right dependencies, platforms and a forward-thinking database schema.

I been building an incredible amount of custom infra, admin pages, cli's to help both me and the agents and that work did speed me up so much. Would have never done that with the old ways.

Bigger changes alwats get tests. Automated ones usually aren't great, but the model almost always finds issues when you ask it to write tests IN THE SAME CONTEXT. Context is prescious, don't waste it.

Even removed my last MCP, since Claude sometimes would go off spinning up Playwright unasked when it could simply read the code - which is faster and pollutes the context less.

Pick services that have cli's: vercel, psql, gh, axiom. Agents can use them, one line in claude md is enough "logs: axiom or vercel cli". "Databsase: psql + one example how to load env corretly so the loop is faster"

Got an insane amout done with this setup. Other cli's/models still don't come close. codex can't search (asking "google best practices" is usually better than context7. cursor/GPT-5 takes FOREVER and doesn't share it's thinking, so I's hard to steer. GPT-5 also is much more literall in how you have to prompt it - it's a great model but not the best agent, you have to be more precise and specific.

Still don't see how this could be moved to background agents. I steer the models a lot as I notice them drifting off - that's much harder if they run in the background.

The new rate limits will go into effect August 28 and that'll definitely suck. Guess I'll just pay up. No perfect alternative for now.

(Big cleanup/migration day eve here)

text:
我表哥拿到外地公司的录用通知，月薪一万八。

他还没来得及回复，妻子已经用家里的公共邮箱替他回了邮件：

感谢认可，但我们家庭安排不允许。

表哥是在对方人事打电话催确认时，才知道这件事。

他回家问妻子为什么不跟他商量。

妻子说，孩子刚上小学，房贷还在还，你去了外地，难道家里三个人都跟着你搬？你妈现在每周还要去医院，谁接送？

表哥说，外地工作虽然辛苦，但一年能多挣十几万，干两年就能把房贷压力降下来。

妻子冷笑了一下：你只看见多挣十几万，没看见家里每天少一个人。

表哥说，那我先去报到，周末再回来，孩子和老人我一起想办法。

妻子把他的行李箱推回卧室，说你想去就去，但别把所有后果都推给我。

表哥没再争，晚上收拾了两套衣服，又把车挂到了二手平台，准备卖车换路费。

第二天早上，他刚到公司，外地那边的人事又打来电话。

原来的岗位已经给了别人，但可以安排他去另一个城市，薪资少四千，三天内确认。

表哥回家时，妻子正在厨房算账。

她把一张纸推到他面前，上面写着孩子补课、房贷、婆婆看病和每个月的生活费。

她说：你真去了，车卖不卖都不够折腾。你自己想清楚，别到时候回来怪我。

表哥没有接那张纸，拿出手机准备回复对方。

这时银行发来一条提醒，他们的房贷即将重新定价，需要补交家庭收入证明。

妻子已经把自己的工资流水、孩子的户口资料和表哥以前的收入证明都上传了，备注里写着：

家庭成员暂不接受异地工作安排。

银行最后还缺他本人确认。

表哥盯着那行字看了很久，关掉了外地公司的邮件。

妻子以为他答应了，转身去给孩子热牛奶。

表哥拿起手机，把那份家庭收入证明撤回，重新打开了外地公司的确认页面。

这一次，他没有先告诉妻子。

text:
我们小区的真事儿。

楼上的小情侣papa声音太大，而且是在凌晨两点多，估计是夜场之类上班的，每天凌晨一回来就干这种事情，嗷嗷叫。

楼下的老头儿经常在凌晨被吵醒，交涉了很多次以后，两小年轻还是不改正，脸皮厚的很，报警也没用，那时候还没立法噪音问题，估计警察也不好硬处理，或则只想和稀泥。

然后老头儿一看既然都不管，他的骚操作来了，直接录音，然后把这个录音导入那种跳广场舞的大音响里，等小情侣每天一回来，老头儿就把这个大音响用根棍子伸出窗外。

整个小区就开始“嗷嗷啊”的叫，不，应该说我们这个片区的夜空都在嗷嗷叫。

这下子轮到小情侣两个懵逼了，所有小区的邻居也开始疯狂报警J。

但奈何老头儿80多岁的人了，法抗拉满，警察也只能劝和为主。

就这么折腾了四五个来回，硬是把两小情侣赶走了。

text:
平时每月 500 多美金的 AWS 账单，9 月才过 7 天，直接被刷到 6,600 多美金。

凌晨收到邮件，账号被停用了。元凶是两台完全不认识的 c5.2xlarge，一周跑了 70TB 出站流量，典型的被人拿去当代理节点卖带宽。

顺着 CloudTrail 一查，实锤了：

我的 IAM 密钥泄露，攻击者用脚本连开五波实例，来源 IP 全是美国住宅宽带。

最细思极恐的是，账号停用前几分钟，他还创建了一个叫 bedrock-console-4 的 IAM 用户，名字伪装成 AWS 官方服务，就差一步做成持久化后门了。

泄露源查到最后，挺无奈的：

我平时会用一些第三方模型 API 中转站，key 大概率是对话的时候带出去的。（建议大家一定要用官方 AI 做这些安全敏感的事情）

这种事真的防不胜防，自己本地做得再规范，也堵不住别人那里的口子。

说实话，干了这么多年 DevOps，攻防演练做过，安全审计也做过，自以为底线意识足够强了。

结果栽在这样一个“新型 AI 诈骗”上。

不过这次止损全程是多亏了 AI 陪我做完的：

取证、画时间线、删后门、终止实例、轮换密钥、起草欺诈申诉，一环扣一环。

换以前自己一个人查，光 CloudTrail 就得啃一整天。

几个血泪教训：

1. 密钥当成消耗品，定期轮换，别指望一把 key 用一辈子。

2. 给第三方服务的 key 权限最小化，能用只读就别给写，能用单桶就别给全账号。

3. MFA 管的是控制台，Access Key 泄露等于门钥匙被人复制，第一时间禁用。

4. AWS 对密钥泄露产生的欺诈账单是可以申诉减免的，证据链一定留好。

最后要专门夸一下 AWS 官方。

提交证据申诉之后，他们确认了属于密钥泄露盗刷，这 6,600 多美金的费用愿意撤销，账号也在走解封流程。

没有跟我扯皮，处理得干脆利落，这点真的值得点赞。

有惊无险，上了最贵的一课，但也算遇到了最体面的处理。

text:
一大批做 Agent 基础设施的公司，今天都该重新看一遍自己的护城河了。

OpenAI 今天发布了 Agents API，把 Codex 背后那套 Agent harness 直接开放出来了。

以前你想做一个真正能干活的 Agent，光接模型远远不够。你还得自己处理长任务怎么一直跑、上下文爆了怎么办、几十个工具怎么选、任务失败怎么恢复、多个子 Agent 怎么分工、代码到底放在哪个沙箱里执行。

现在开发者给任务、模型、工具和运行环境，Agents API 负责会话编排、上下文压缩、工具调用和多 Agent 协作。甚至可以直接把任务扔给 Codex 同款 harness 跑几小时甚至几天。

我觉得这件事对 Agent 行业的影响会很直接。

过去很多所谓的 Agent 创业公司，本质上卖的就是给模型套一层壳，接工具，管上下文，再做一套工作流编排。

现在模型厂商开始把这些东西做成基础能力了。

如果你的产品价值还停留在「我能让模型调用十几个工具」「我能让几个 Agent 一起工作」，那这个故事已经越来越难讲。

最后真正还能留下价值的，大概率会往两头走：

一头是 E2B、Cloudflare、Vercel、Modal 这种真正提供运行环境的基础设施；

另一头是掌握行业数据、权限和真实工作流的垂直应用。

Agent 的门槛又被打低了一截。

这个自称跨亚裔的女生吐槽，她在一家中餐馆用餐时被歧视了，服务员把她误认成白人还提供了叉子。

​她直言，自己去这家中餐馆就是为了确认自己的跨亚裔身份认同，点了一碗牛肉捞面，一开始都一切正常。

​可当她准备用筷子吃饭时，服务员却拿了一把叉子过来，这显然是觉得她不会用筷子，因为她看起来不像亚裔。

​她当时很震惊，没想到在自己以为的安全空间里，还是遇到了这种仅凭外貌就认定她是白人的身份歧视。

​她把服务员叫过来，说明自己是华裔，这种被误认的感觉让她很受伤。她坚持要把这碗面退回去，拒绝让叉子抹去自己的跨亚裔身份。

text:
某个 Shopify 团队在做内部工具，创始人兼 CEO Tobi 两周后才得知此事，强力介入并把项目掉头 ？

Tobi 正面回应了这个传闻，也让我们看到了 Shopify 这个知名团队创始人的工作方式：
Founder-mode-as-a-service！

1. 那个被砍掉的架构确实该砍。 Tobi 把原方案形容为“cosplaying an enterprise production app”：团队给内部工具搭了 headless Rails + GraphQL API + React 单页应用的前后端分离架构，结果连改个小功能都需要前端工程师介入。他的判断是：内部工具就该用朴素的 Rails 全栈（服务端渲染、单仓库、一人可改全栈）。这是典型的“架构凭空过度设计”，为想象中的规模和复杂度设计，而非实际需求。

2. 这类干预往往是一线团队主动请他做的。 Tobi 说自己经常做这种裁定，通常是因为有团队成员私下请他出手；想砍掉过度设计的一方需要一个“唱黑脸的人”，而他愿意在认同前提时扮演这个角色，省掉无休止的会议和变革管理流程。Shopify 内部戏称这项服务为 "Founder-mode-as-a-service"。

3. 他不只裁决，还做“决策复盘”。 十年来他持续做一档内部播客叫 Context，回头讲解这些决策当时的推理过程，目的是教会其他人以后不需要他也能做出同样的判断。他顺带点出这背后的敌人是沉没成本谬误，团队倾向于因为“已经投入这么多”而继续错的方向，而复盘机制就是为了对抗这一点。

4. 对“Shopify 是尽管有他干预才成功”的说法，他不接受。 他认为反过来才成立：公司的成功正因为这类干预。他称“两周后 tobi 才得知……”这种叙事是胡扯，并说那次项目掉头是他最成功的干预之一。他用一句很有担当的话收尾：“让公司保持高效、低技术债，这就是我作为 CEO 的本职工作；所以，罪名成立。” 最后他补了一刀：这类流传的故事之所以受欢迎，只是因为它们比承认“团队确实需要有人来叫停愚蠢的过度架构”更有趣，是更好的“cope stories”。

quotedTweet.text:
Yep. Except:

1. This was about important internal tools. The team was stuck in some architecture nightmare of their own doing (writing it in rails but headless, with graphql api, and a SPA react app, constantly needing frontend engineers for changes). I call this kind of thing 'cosplaying an enterprise production app'. All that complexity was in the way and using straight rails was perfect in that case.

2. I make calls like this all the time. Usually someone on the team asks me to. They see what needs to happen but don’t want to be the bad guy. I’m happy to just make the call if I agree with the premise. Saves enormous amounts of meetings and change management etc. Sometimes this is jokingly referred to as Founder-mode-as-a-service here.

3. For ten years I’ve also run an internal podcast called Context, where I revisit decisions like these and explain the reasoning so everyone can learn from them. This is helpful to give people all the variables that were considered and why this was the choice made given the information available at the time. I want to teach how to make such decisions effectively without needing me. Sunk cost fallacy is a problem.

4. Any notions that Shopify is succcessful despite of me doing this, instead of because of it, will have a hard time making their argument come together I think 😄

the part of 'two weeks later tobi learns about...' is nonsese and the pivot of that project up there happens one of the more successful examples of interventions. But getting the company to work effectively with great architecture and low technical debt baggage into the right direction is literally the job, so guilty as charged I suppose.

But there are always cope stories floating around like this because they are more fun, than saying 'somehow we needed tobi to stop doing silly architecture astronautics'.  I can totally see that.

朋友开了一家饭店，雇佣了一对小夫妻，男方是厨师，女方是服务员。

男方薪水为8000元，女方薪水为3000元。经过开业三个月饭店差不多回本了。

由于男厨师的烹饪技艺出色，女服务员的服务也让顾客很满意，因此回头客占到了60％以上。

饭店老板娘和女服务员同时在场时，顾客也会直接找女服务员点菜开酒。然而，那位女服务员开始觉得自己比较吃香，于是和她的丈夫一起找朋友要求每人涨薪
2000元否则就不干了。他们还说假如当初他们有创业资金，就会自己开一家店。

现在我朋友为难了，不涨薪的话饭店的生意就靠他们俩，但如果涨了薪水，又担心他们下次再提涨薪怎么办？太难了！

quotedTweet.text:
A correction is overdue about what actually happened in the North Carolina "5-in-5" case.

On August 5, Darren Heitner and Ryan Downton's Texas Trial Group told the public that the NCAA had misled the court, falsely characterized their case as involving antitrust law, and deprived 54 college athletes of their scheduled hearing through improper judge shopping.

That is, at minimum, a remarkably incomplete account of what happened. The chronology matters.

At 1:31 PM, the Texas Trial Group account posted: "We're not in NC having our hearing today because the @NCAA mislead the court. Here's what the NCAA filed to avoid our hearing. Our case was breach of contract, not antitrust. And our second claim, under N.C.G.S. 75-1.1, is explicitly excluded from the business court jurisdiction" (emphasis added). 

At 1:57 PM, Heitner quote-posted that and went further. The NCAA's representation that the case involved an antitrust dispute was, he wrote, "A FALSE STATEMENT" (emphasis added). He accused the NCAA of moving the case "to a judge it believed would rule in its favor," and declared: "Lying to shop judges is unethical at its core" (emphasis added). There would be no hearing in North Carolina, he said, and the plaintiffs may file elsewhere.

But at 2:08:03 PM — 37 minutes after the first post, 11 minutes after the second — plaintiffs' own North Carolina counsel filed a Notice of Voluntary Dismissal Without Prejudice as to all claims against the NCAA. Six days after the complaint.

Read that again.

* The Business Court did not dismiss these athletes' claims.
* The NCAA did not obtain an order denying them a preliminary injunction.
* A Business Court judge did not refuse to hear them.
* The North Carolina Supreme Court did not prevent them from proceeding.
* The plaintiffs dismissed their own lawsuit.

To be precise, Business Court designation explains why the hearing originally scheduled before the Guilford County Superior Court judge did not occur there that afternoon on August 5th. Fair enough. But designation did not kill the case. It changed the forum in which the case would proceed.

Importantly, the plaintiffs remained free to challenge designation. They could seek expedited consideration. They could ask the Business Court for emergency relief. They could brief the merits. They could obtain a ruling from a Business Court judge whom the NCAA itself had no power to select. Instead, their own counsel voluntarily dismissed the entire action six days after filing it.

That distinction matters when lawyers publicly accuse opposing counsel of "lying," "judge shopping," and unethical conduct.

You can believe the NCAA's designation was wrong. You can argue that § 75-1.1 did not provide a basis for Business Court jurisdiction. You can criticize designation for disrupting a hearing that had been scheduled for August 5. Those are legitimate legal arguments.

But telling the public that the NCAA's supposed misconduct was the reason these 54 athletes would not be heard — while omitting that the plaintiffs themselves voluntarily terminated the North Carolina action that same afternoon — creates a materially different impression from what the court record actually shows.

They portrayed reassignment to one of North Carolina's most sophisticated courts as though it were the functional dismissal of their clients' claims. Then, 11 minutes later, their own side accomplished the actual dismissal.

Moreover, North Carolina law doesn't require a cause of action captioned "antitrust" before a case can be designated to the Business Court. NCGS § 7A-45.4 asks whether an action involves "a material issue related to" one of the enumerated categories. The NCAA filed a standard notice of designation with the Chief Justice of the North Carolina Supreme Court, who designated the case and assigned it to the Business Court. That is the routine mechanism, used in North Carolina every week.

As for the claim that § 75-1.1 is "explicitly excluded," the Texas Trial Group attached the standard form that answers it. Category (3) reaches disputes arising under Chapter 75 that "do not arise solely under NCGS § 75-1.1 or Article 2 of Chapter 75." By plaintiffs' own account, their case was principally a breach of contract action with a § 75-1.1 claim alongside it. The carveout is for disputes arising solely under that section. Theirs, on their own telling, did not.

Some context for readers outside North Carolina. The Business Court isn't a procedural backwater where defendants send lawsuits to disappear. It is the North Carolina's specialized forum for complex commercial litigation, staffed by Special Superior Court Judges who handle sophisticated, high-stakes cases. Contested motions proceed through full written briefing — opening brief, response, reply — and are resolved by detailed written opinions. Final judgments bypass the Court of Appeals and go directly to the North Carolina Supreme Court. And the designating party doesn't choose the judge.

Whether the NCAA's designation would have survived a challenge is a question no one will ever answer, because plaintiffs dismissed rather than raise it. 

What can be said is that calling a routine designation notice a lie, and the lawyers who filed it judge-shoppers, was an extraordinarily serious accusation— made, as it turns out, minutes before those 54 athletes lost their case in North Carolina at their own lawyers' hands.

How to post-train a model to personalize it on your code repo? In our latest research in Bespoke Labs, we post-trained a model to improve its performance on a given Github repository. 

Starting from Inkling base,  we use supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with trajectories coming from a strong teacher model, and reinforcement learning (GRPO) on repository-specialized environments that we curated. SFT gave a 52pp improvement in performance on the held-out fontTools evaluation set. Further RL training lifts the total improvement to 57pp compared to the base Inkling model.

In addition to the in-distribution evaluation our post-trained Inkling shows good performance on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Lite while becoming 40% more token efficient due to post-training. 

Read our full research blog post here:
https://t.co/i9Xj0siSRb

Many thanks to Thinking Machines Lab for their credit contribution that helped support this research.

The systems that saved me. The discipline that drove me. The meaning that kept me moving. 

Nearly 40,000 words later, I can finally say it:  

I'm a published author.

text:
The reverb from 9/11 reached far and wide. And it included the death of soldiers deployed to the Middle East after the U.S. events to defend our nation against those who attacked us on that awful day. 

I knew one of them. His beautiful young wife was a colleague. He had two very young sons he adored. He was 29 years old. 

As I stood beside Jeannine on 9/11 watching on television in horror as the towers fell, we had no idea that just months later what we could barely comprehend from afar would eventually hit her household directly.  

On this day, I still pray for all impacted in New York, D.C., and Pennsylvania on that darkest of days. And equally for those military families scattered across our nation, who in the immediate years after received that dreaded knock on their doors with the saddest of news: “We regret to inform you…”

May God continue to bless and heal those who loved them all. 

Thank you, Sgt. 1st Class Christopher R. Willoughby, for your service and sacrifice. I have never forgotten the price you and your precious family paid for my family’s safety and security.
